smell: SafeRemoveWithLogger accepts ctx but discards it (`_ context.Context`). The body issues os.Stat / os.RemoveAll which can stall indefinitely on a slow / hung NFS or stuck mount during destroy — the long-running operation a destroy ctx is supposed to cancel. Either thread ctx through (Go 1.25 has no ctx-aware RemoveAll, so the canonical fix is to wrap the call in WaitFor + a ctx-cancel race) or drop the parameter so callers don't expect cancellation honoured.
severity_reason: Realistic but bounded: Stat/RemoveAll on a local fs returns fast; only an NFS / stuck mount during okdctl destroy would stretch shutdown unbounded. No data-loss path triggered.
fix_summary: Either: (a) drop the ctx parameter (the four call sites in cleanup.go are sequential and don't supply cancellation expectations), or (b) before each os.RemoveAll, do `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return err }`. (a) is honest about what the function does; (b) costs ~3 lines and gives a destroy ctx a meaningful cancel point.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency: "context.Background()/context.TODO() in production code needs a justification comment" — corollary: a discarded ctx parameter is a worse smell than a Background ctx because the signature lies
Uber §Goroutine Lifetime — cancellation should reach the work that takes time

smell: ValidateIgnitionFiles checks `ctx.Err()` once at function entry, then loops over three files reading + json.Unmarshal-ing each. A ctx cancellation arriving mid-loop is ignored until the loop ends. The ignition files are typically small (<1 MiB) so the practical leak is short, but the pattern "check ctx once, then ignore it" is the same shape as the time.Sleep-in-retry pattern CLAUDE.md §concurrency calls out.
severity_reason: 3-file fixed bound, ~MB read each — total work bounded to a few seconds. Below blocker/major rubric anchors. Pattern smell rather than a real leak.
fix_summary: Add a `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return err }` at the top of the for-loop body. Three lines, makes the cancellation contract honest.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/orchestrator.go:77-82 — Run() does the same check between steps

smell: InjectCustomManifests accepts `_ context.Context` and loops copying files via system.CopyFile. The number of files is user-controlled (whatever lives under automation/config/manifests) so the loop is unbounded in principle. If a deploy is cancelled mid-inject, the loop runs to completion. Same shape as ValidateIgnitionFiles.
severity_reason: Practical risk is low: typical automation/config/manifests has <10 files. Below minor anchor.
fix_summary: Rename `_ context.Context` → `ctx context.Context` and add `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return count, err }` at top of the loop body.

smell: InstallToolsToSystem accepts `_ context.Context` and loops over three large binaries (oc, openshift-install, kubectl can be hundreds of MB combined) calling system.CopyFile + system.MakeExecutable. CopyFile + permission mutation on multi-hundred-MB binaries is several-second work; a ctx cancel arriving here is ignored. The function is on the deploy hot path (tools-download → install).
severity_reason: Real (multi-hundred-MB copies stretch shutdown) but bounded to ~3 binaries, only on the deploy path. Below the major rubric anchor.
fix_summary: Thread ctx: rename param to `ctx context.Context` and add `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return err }` at the top of the for-loop body. system.CopyFile already accepts no ctx; once it gains one (or is replaced with an io.Copy under a ctx-aware reader), thread that too.
rule_source: Uber §Goroutine Lifetime — cancellation should reach the work that takes time

smell: startMetricsServer's stop closure builds `shutCtx` with `context.Background()` even though the caller (executeFullDeployment) has a ctx in hand. The ctx-from-caller would be cancelled by SIGINT first, which is exactly what we don't want here (we want the 5-second graceful drain to run after parent ctx cancel). So Background is *correct* — but there is no comment justifying it, which CLAUDE.md §concurrency requires ("`context.Background()` / `context.TODO()` in production code needs a justification comment").
severity_reason: Comment-policy nit, not a behaviour bug. The Background choice is correct; the gap is documentation.
fix_summary: Add a one-line comment above `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ...)` explaining: "Use Background, not the caller's ctx, so the 5s graceful drain runs even after SIGINT cancelled the parent." Same wording as monitor.go's reapTimer comment.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency: "`context.Background()` / `context.TODO()` in production code needs a justification comment — almost every call site should be receiving a ctx from its caller"

smell: The shell-completion ValidArgsFunction passes context.Background() to fetcher.FetchVersions. cobra exposes a Context-bearing variant via the (cmd, args, toComplete) signature — completion can get cmd.Context() which honours the user's Ctrl-C. Today, a hung GitHub call during tab-completion blocks the shell until the underlying http client's own timeout fires.
severity_reason: Tab completion only — not a deploy-time path. Inconvenience, not correctness.
fix_summary: Change the closure to `func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string, _ string)` and call `fetcher.FetchVersions(cmd.Context())`. Adds proper cancellation if the user Ctrl-C's during completion.
rule_source: cobra docs — ValidArgsFunction signature accepts the command, which carries a Context

smell: printUpdateNotice uses `case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond)` in a select. Bare time.After leaks the underlying Timer until it fires (per CLAUDE.md, the canonical alternative is time.NewTimer + Stop on the win path). Here the cap is 100ms and the function is called once at process exit, so the 'leak' has zero observable cost — but the pattern is the one the doc calls out.
severity_reason: 100ms one-shot at process exit — no real leak. Pure consistency / pattern-hygiene improvement.
fix_summary: Replace with: `t := time.NewTimer(100 * time.Millisecond); defer t.Stop(); select { case result = <-ch: case <-t.C: return }`. Two extra lines for pattern consistency with internal/distribution/okd/install/monitor.go's reapTimer.
rule_source: Go proverb: "don't use time.After in a long-lived select" — this isn't long-lived but the idiom propagates

smell: MonitorInstallation is the most concurrency-dense function in the codebase: a Wait-reaper goroutine, a sync.OnceFunc kill, a CSR-approval ticker, a reap timer with deadline, and a select with three cases. internal/system/exec_test.go already uses Go 1.25 testing/synctest (six tests covering WaitFor). Identical patterns in MonitorInstallation have NO tests — this is the canonical synctest opportunity per audit-concurrency rule catalog.
severity_reason: Test gap, not a code defect. audit-tests is the actual owner of "this path has no test" findings — flagging here only for the synctest-opportunity rule.
fix_summary: Add monitor_test.go using `synctest.Test` to fake the openshift-install subprocess (extract a `wait()` interface to inject), advance virtual time across the CSRApprovalInterval, and assert: (a) ticker tick triggers ApprovePendingCSRs, (b) ctx-cancel triggers killInstall + reapTimer race, (c) reap-timeout path logs the abandon message. The exec_test.go pattern is the template.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/system/exec_test.go (six synctest tests on the WaitFor patterns)

smell: Provider.Connect and Provider.Disconnect each accept `_ context.Context` for interface symmetry but never use it. Connect's body is pure validation + struct mutation (no I/O happens until Provision). The CLAUDE.md scaffolding-as-roadmap rule (MEMORY.md §scaffolding) covers this: the ctx is API scaffolding for the symmetric Connect/Disconnect shape used by future providers (the alternative would be a Connect signature without ctx, which then breaks symmetry with a network-bound Connect on a hypothetical AWS provider). Keep the param, but flag for review.
severity_reason: Scaffolding-as-roadmap: Connect/Disconnect is the symmetric API a future provider (AWS, Azure) would implement; both will have ctx-using bodies. MEMORY.md says keep, severity capped at suggestion.
fix_summary: Verify intent: keep the ctx parameter on the Connect/Disconnect contract. No code change required. (Optionally add a comment: "// ctx accepted for symmetry with future network-bound providers; this implementation is local-only.")
rule_source: repo-counter-example: addon.Addon has Install(ctx)/Uninstall(ctx) for the same symmetry reason

smell: BackgroundCheck spawns a goroutine that writes to a buffered chan; the caller race-reads the chan against time.After(100ms). If runCheck still has an in-flight HTTP call when the 100ms expires, the goroutine remains alive until the http client's 4s timeout fires (httpTimeout). The buffered chan means the abandoned send never blocks, so the goroutine reaps cleanly. CLAUDE.md §concurrency calls this exact pattern out as the canonical fire-and-forget shape ("100ms wait at caller is the canonical example"). The leak bound is documented (httpTimeout = 4s). Flagging for visibility, not action.
severity_reason: Documented canonical pattern. Not a finding — captured to make the goroutine inventory complete.
fix_summary: No change. This is the canonical bounded-leak pattern called out in CLAUDE.md. Listed in the goroutine inventory only so the audit footer's coverage statement is honest.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency: "See internal/version/updatecheck.go (100ms wait at caller) for the canonical example."
